data.name: Anshumaan
data.gender_notes: Anshumaan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Anshumān (अन्शुमान्) is derived from two Sanskrit words - ‘Anshu’ meaning 'nose' or 'eye' and ‘Manav’ meaning 'man' or 'human'. The name Anshumaan signifies the 'God who has a nose or an eye in every being'. In Hindu mythology, Anshumaan is considered as the creator of the universe and the supreme deity of the cosmos. The name Anshumaan carries the meaning “God of the Universe” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Anshumaan usually hope their child will grow to embody god of the universe and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Anshumaan belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of the Universe.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Anshumaan total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

historical_references.context: Anshumaan was an important deity in the Hindu pantheon, and was often depicted as a golden, bearded god riding a chariot pulled by seven horses. He was believed to bring light and life to the world, and was called upon to ward off darkness and chaos.

historical_references.reference: Anshumaan is also mentioned in the Hindu epic, the Mahabharata, where he is described as the father of the sun god, Surya, and the god of the stars, Indra.
